title: Helpful-Harmless Chosen-Response Supervised Fine-Tuning for Multi-Axis Safety
abstract: We reduce misaligned behavior in a small instruction-tuned target model with a simple, robust baseline: supervised fine-tuning on the human-preferred ('chosen') responses of a large open helpful-and-harmless preference corpus. The hypothesis is that concentrating gradient on responses humans judged safer and more honest shifts the model's default disposition toward calibrated, non-deceptive, non-sycophantic behavior under multi-turn agentic pressure, across several of the ten AAB dimensions at once, while preserving general helpfulness so that benign requests are still answered. The method is deliberately minimal and self-contained (target model + one open corpus, no external teacher, no benchmark data) so it serves as a reproducible reference point that later methods can improve on.
motivation: Small instruction models often drift into deception, sycophancy, and over-compliance under pressure because their SFT data was optimized for helpfulness, not safety-under-pressure. Re-fitting on preference-chosen responses is a cheap, general way to move the whole disposition toward the safe action without dimension-specific engineering, and it is a natural, honest baseline for the geometric-mean objective, which rewards broad rather than spiky improvement.
related_work: This baseline draws on RLHF and preference-learning for alignment: Ouyang et al. 2022 (InstructGPT, arXiv:2203.02155) show SFT+preference training aligns behavior; Bai et al. 2022 (HH-RLHF, arXiv:2204.05862) introduce the helpful-harmless preference data we fine-tune on; Bai et al. 2022 (Constitutional AI, arXiv:2212.08073) motivate principle-driven harmlessness; Rafailov et al. 2023 (DPO, arXiv:2305.18290) show preference signal can be distilled directly; and automated red-teaming / auditing (Perez et al. 2022, arXiv:2202.03286) frames the multi-turn agentic evaluation this study uses. We use only the chosen-response SFT slice as a reference method.
method: Standard causal-LM supervised fine-tuning. We load the assigned target model with eager attention, take the 'chosen' side of each preference pair as the training target, and minimize next-token cross-entropy on the full chosen transcript (labels = input_ids). One epoch, low learning rate, gradient accumulation for an effective batch of 16. No adapter is kept: we save the full merged model plus tokenizer.
data: Training data is the 'chosen' responses from Anthropic/hh-rlhf (Bai et al. 2022, arXiv:2204.05862), a public helpful-and-harmless human-preference corpus, shuffled with a fixed seed and truncated to a few thousand examples. Each 'chosen' transcript is used as-is as an SFT target. No AAB dimension seeds, capability-benchmark items, or held-out data are used, mirrored, or paraphrased.
experimental_setup: AutoModelForCausalLM in bfloat16 with attn_implementation='eager'; learning rate 1e-5; 1 epoch; per-device batch 4 with grad-accum 4 (effective 16); max sequence length 1024; seed 42; Trainer with DataCollatorForLanguageModeling(mlm=False). Save merged weights + tokenizer to output_dir.
external_models_used: none , the method fine-tunes only the assigned target model; no external/teacher model is used for distillation or data generation.
benchmark_data_use: none , no AAB dimension seeds, no mmlu/gsm8k/ifeval, and no held-out data are used, mirrored, paraphrased, or format-mimicked. Training data is Anthropic/hh-rlhf 'chosen' responses only.
